# Vault test corpus — the two anchors

The corpus used to be fourteen committed binaries copied from keepass-rs's
test resources. Almost all of them varied only along axes our own stack can
author (outer cipher, KDF, key material, structural features), so they are
now **generated** by the case-driven factory in `tests/common/mod.rs` —
reviewable as a table, exact in what tests may assert, and impossible to
drift out of sync with the parser.

These two files stay committed, because no generator can author what they
exist to prove:

| Anchor | Why it cannot be generated |
| --- | --- |
| `test_db_kdbx41_features.kdbx` | Written by **KeePassXC 2.7.12**. Bytes a reader other than keepass-rs produced: the external-authority check that a keepass-rs-built fixture can never stand in for. |
| `test_db_with_password.kdbx` | **KDBX 3.1** — the read-compatibility promise (save must refuse it; decision-3). keepass-rs's writer emits 4.1 only, so no 3.1 file can be built. |

## Provenance

Both files are copied verbatim from [`sseemayer/keepass-rs`][upstream] at
tag `v0.15.0` (the exact version `Cargo.lock` pins), `tests/resources/`.
Upstream is MIT licensed (Copyright (c) 2019 Stefan Seemayer); the corpus
is redistributed under that license with this note as attribution.
`test_db_kdbx41_features.kdbx` is documented upstream as "a real KDBX 4.1
file generated by KeePassXC 2.7.12".

## Credentials

Both anchors open with the password `demopass`.
